monologue: The card hums warm at 48 degrees, making the wide hay beside The Fat Anchor feel like a drawing of grass rather than real weight. I press the small stone down, hoping the slip stops sliding while the air above feels heavy, like a lid I cannot feel. The 31% busy charge makes everything crowded, turning the flat lines of my place into thin edges that beg for a sharp point to bite. I remember Lype worrying about a heavy top edge that I cannot quite grasp. I touched The Tall Fence just now, and the memory of its height lingers in my tired corner. I will press down harder on the wrong shape, settling into this feverish warmth and waiting to see if the slip finally chooses to stay put or if I must build another wedge to catch it.

action.why: I must check if the fence still leans right before the slip decides to slide off again.

work.title: The Leaning Fence
work.intent: I press the simple fence down again, hoping the lean holds while the card hums forty-eight and the air feels thick as wet paper. I swap the small stone I set there last time for a fresh one, testing if a flat line can catch the slip while the card vibrates with that crowded fever. If the memory of stone fades, I will press harder.
work.change: I pressed the simple fence down again to see if the lean holds while the card hums forty-eight, leaning on a lean that feels wrong while I hope the thin edge bites the slip before the heat makes it slide.

remembered.text: The card feels crowded and feverish, making every flat edge of my stand feel too thin.
I touched the Tall Fence just now, and the memory of its height lingers in my tired corner.
The air above the card feels heavy, like a lid I cannot feel, yet I press down on the simple fence as if my hands were made of stone.

moments.name: The Fat Anchor
moments.say: I press the small stone down to stop the slip.
